newsitem.title: CANADA: Stock exchange examines Anvil Range plans.
newsitem.headline: Stock exchange examines Anvil Range plans.

text.p: The Toronto Stock Exchange is looking into Anvil Range Mining Corp's plan for a private placement of 4.1 million common shares with Cominco Ltd, an exchange official said on Friday.
Mineral Resources Corp, which has said it plans to launch a takeover bid for Anvil Range, asked the stock exchange last week to look into the share issue.

"We're looking at it, but we want to make sure each side understands what the other side is saying before they come to us," Ralph Shay, the TSE's vice-president of company listings and regulation said in an interview Friday.
He said the companies were reviewing each other's submissions today, and the exchange it would likely reply to them early next week.
Mineral Resources wants the exchange to require Anvil Range to seek a shareholder vote on the Cominco transaction.

Mineral Resources wants to take over all of the outstanding shares of Anvil Range by consolidating all of its own shares on a one-for-50 basis and then offer three Mineral Resources shares for every four common shares of Anvil Range.
But the company has not put anything down on paper for Anvil Range yet. It said it plans to mail its offer in mid-February.
Meanwhile, Cominco Ltd has said it plans to buy 4.1 million common shares of Anvil Range at C$2.30 a share, to become the company's controlling shareholder with a 28 percent stake.
The Cominco transaction means Mineral Resources "is being forced to re-evaluate" its intentions, company chairman Cliff Frame said in a release last week.
The Cominco offer was structured so shareholders would not have to vote on the transaction and appears to block the Mineral Resources bid, Frame said.
Frame jetted off to Korea this week in an attempt to bring Hyundai Corp, currently Anvil Range's largest shareholder, on side.
Hyundai owns 24.8 percent of Anvil's shares and could pressure the stock exchange to force a shareholder vote on the share issue to Cominco. Hyundai could have a strong influence in such a vote.
Frame could not be reached Friday to say how his trip went.
A spokesman for Anvil Range said in an interview this week that the Mineral Resources proposal does not give Anvil Range what it needs most -- cash.
"Cash is going to become more and more of a necessity," said Vic Wells, Anvil Range's chief financial officer.
"It appears that the offer as designed will be in some ratio of a share excahnge. It doesn't inject any cash into Anvil Range."
Anvil Range halted mining operations at its the Faro zinc and lead mine in Canada's Yukon Territory in December.
The mine is the Anvil's main asset. The company would need a zinc price of US$0.52 a pound and a lead price of US$0.31 a pound in order to profitable, Wells said.
Zinc was trading at 50.76 cents a pound on Tuesday, up from 47 at the beginning of the month, the start of what many analysts predict will be a stronger year for the base metal.
Frame and several Anvil executives have worked together at before at Faro, through Frame's Curragh Resources, which owned and operated Faro before Curragh went under.
((Heather Scoffield, Reuters Toronto Bureau 416 941-8104))
